name: Unit Vectors
description: Learn about Unit Vectors and its applications in physics.

content.overview: Ever seen a signpost that just says "this way" with an arrow, no distance on it? That's basically a unit vector - all direction, no size. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: A unit vector has magnitude exactly 1 - it represents pure direction {{viz:diagram-02}}
To get one: v̂ = v / |v| (divide the vector by its own magnitude)
î, ĵ, k̂ are the standard unit vectors along the x, y, and z axes
content.whyItMatters: Unit vectors are how physics keeps 'direction' and 'size' cleanly separated. Whenever you write a force, velocity, or field as (magnitude) × (unit vector), you're using this trick - and it shows up in nearly every chapter after this one.
